titulo: Dative 2: verbs that take the dative: Gefallen, schmecken, passen and others

aula.titulo: Dative 2: verbs that take the dative
aula.objetivo: Use the verbs that put the person in the dative (helfen, danken, gehören, gefallen, schmecken, passen, fehlen, antworten, gratulieren, glauben) and the "how I feel" expressions with «mir» and «dir».

blocos.titulo: Gefallen, schmecken, passen: the German way of "liking"
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «gefallen» flips the sentence: the person who likes goes into the DATIVE and the thing they like is the subject: «Das Kleid gefällt mir» — literally "the dress pleases me" = I like the dress. English does the same with "please" and "appeal to": "the dress appeals to me". STEP 2: the verb agrees with the THING: «Die Schuhe gefallen mir» (plural — "the shoes please me"). STEP 3: «schmecken» is about taste: «Die Suppe schmeckt mir (gut)» (I like the soup). STEP 4: «passen» means "to fit" and "to suit": «Die Jacke passt mir» (the jacket fits me), «Die Farbe passt dir gut» (the color suits you). STEP 5: «fehlen» (to be missing): «Mir fehlt Zeit» (I'm short of time — "time is missing to me"). STEP 6: «glauben», «folgen» and «zuhören» also take the dative for the person: «Ich glaube dir» (I believe you), «Sie folgt ihm» (she follows him), «Hör mir zu!» (listen to me!). STEP 7: «wehtun» (to hurt): «Der Kopf tut mir weh» (my head hurts). Careful: «gefallen» changes a to ä with «er» (es gefällt).

erros.motivo: The person who likes goes into the dative.
The verb agrees with the THING that is liked.

blocos.enunciado: Say 6 sentences about what you like: «Das Haus gefällt mir. Die Suppe schmeckt mir. Die Jacke passt mir.»
Write one sentence with each verb from the previous session.
